messages.text: Mahomes makes winning return as Chiefs storm past Broncos

metadata.summary: Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on debut while Patrick Mahomes made his return from knee surgery as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night.
metadata.content: Patrick Mahomes returns from knee injury as Kansas City Chiefs storm past Denver Broncos | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to content Patrick Mahomes returns from knee injury as Kansas City Chiefs storm past Denver Broncos Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker stars on his Kansas City Chiefs debut with the most rushing yards by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles in 2012, posting 173 and two touchdowns; Walker signed with the Chiefs in free agency after guiding the Seattle Seahawks to Super Bowl glory Tuesday 15 September 2026 06:27, UK Image: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes was victorious on his return to action Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on debut while Patrick Mahomes made his return from knee surgery as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night. Mahomes did not appear to be affected by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, as he threw for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as AFC West division champions. Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star, who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, also had three catches for 18 yards. messages.text: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes

metadata.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
metadata.content: Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle delves into the talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix, assessing F1's newest venue and where it can be improved, the debate around the rules that cost Lando Norris, and Kimi Antonelli's ever-growing world championship lead Martin Brundle Expert Analyst @MBrundleF1 Monday 14 September 2026 16:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See how Lando Norris lost the lead and a likely win at the Spanish Grand Prix after an untimely Virtual Safety Car for the McLaren driver The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers. It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges. The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.
